benchmark.distinction: All21 pinned host shape/dtype cases use original kernel.warmup with original scalar values, constexpr BLOCK128, pointer/scalar divisibility attributes, and default launch options. These specialized binaries are distinct from the explicitly runtime-i32 generic pilot. Package dispatch/allocation/final casts are not timed.

assumptions: Same-stream initialized output is private until completion; invocation inputs remain live and within allocation bounds.
Original wrapper valid-input domain is retained; no arbitrary pointer aliases or concurrent external observers.
Compilation applies exactly the private-output/disjoint-input contract already implied by this allocation; no unordered-reduction assertion or changed atomic expression.

evidence.fact: Fresh torch.zeros fp32 output is allocated inside the wrapper before the launch.
One launch consumes grad_in and the new output; output is only returned/cast after the launch.
Kernel has one unused-result atomic-add and reads only grad_in. Output is never read by ordinary accesses.

correctness.random_reference: CPU float64 torch.ops.aten.unfold_backward of represented input values; per-destination gamma_(n-1)*sum(abs(x)) error bound; before the wrapper's final dtype conversion

timing.protocol: Shared physical input/output buffers; CUDA graphs capture100 repetitions;9 randomized-order rounds;50ms warmup; medians across rounds. GPU exclusively assigned to this experiment. Clocks not locked.
timing.scope: Output zero reset plus unchanged extracted kernel only. Excludes allocation, final dtype conversion, package dispatch, and full benchmark harness. Seven exact repository benchmark shapes; three dtypes. Small launch-bound cases; not a distribution over the full inventory. Reset-only is separately captured and measured, not subtracted.
